answers.question: You said reads may be retried on timeout without limit. Nothing then ends a read that never answers: the agent would keep reading and the customer would wait forever. What ends it?
answers.recommended: The agent tries a read that gets no answer at most 3 times in all. After the third no answer it does what it does when that read fails: at the start, it tells the customer it cannot see their orders right now and to try again later; after the cancel call, it says the outcome is unknown, issues no refund and hands the case to staff; after the refund calls, it says the refund status is unknown and hands the case to staff.
answers.reply: > Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.

answers.question: You listed "order not found" as an answer of the cancel call. Nothing says what the agent does then. Shortest path: the customer has one open order and asks to cancel it by its number; the agent lists the orders; the agent proposes cancelling it with the refund; the customer says yes; the agent sends the cancel call; the cancel call answers "order not found"; the agent has no next step.
answers.recommended: The agent tells the customer it cannot find that order, changes nothing, and issues no refund.
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> An order number matching none of the customer's orders: the agent says so and changes nothing.

answers.question: After the cancel call gets no answer and a read shows the order still placed or processing, the agent sends the cancel once more under the same confirmation, as you said. Nothing says what it does when that second cancel call also gets no answer and a read again shows the order still open. Shortest path: the customer says yes to the proposal; the cancel call gets no answer and cancelled nothing; the read shows the order still open; the agent sends the cancel once more; that call also gets no answer and cancelled nothing; the read again shows the order still open; the agent has no next step.
answers.recommended: The agent sends no third cancel call, tells the customer the order was not cancelled and no refund was issued, and hands the case to staff.
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> Q4 If the cancel call times out: no blind resend; re-read the order.
> Still placed or processing, send the cancel once more under the same confirmation.

answers.question: Two of your answers disagree in one case. You said that after a refund call with no answer the agent retries once, then re-reads the refund record and reports what it finds; and you accepted that when the refund the order system reports differs from the confirmed amount, the agent tells the customer the amount returned and hands the case to staff. Shortest path: the customer says yes; the order is cancelled; the refund call gets no answer and created nothing; the agent sends the refund call once more; that call answers a refund whose amount differs from the confirmed one; the agent re-reads the refund record; the read gets no answer; the agent tells the customer the refund status is unknown, and never tells them the different amount it was given.
answers.recommended: When the second refund call answers a refund whose amount differs from the confirmed one, the agent acts on that answer at once: it makes no further change, tells the customer the amount the order system returned, and hands the case to staff, without reading the refund again.
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> 3. Cancel succeeded, refund call timed out — state unknown; agent retries once, then re-reads the order and refund records and reports what it finds.
> Final message must match the final refund status.
> For case 3, after the retry the agent re-reads the refund record: pending or issued, report that status; failed or no refund, hand off and say the refund is not confirmed yet; re-read fails, say status unknown and hand off.
